title: Guardrail metrics
reading_md:
**What it is.** Guardrail metrics must not get worse beyond a tolerated margin, even when the success metric improves. Examples are load time, unsubscribes, returns, support contacts and margin. Spotify tests guardrails with non-inferiority tests in its decision rules. The guardrails and their tolerances are set before the test.

**How to work it out.**

Relative change = (treatment - control) / control, compared with the tolerance set in advance

Worked example. Support contacts per 1,000 orders are 20 in control and 23 in treatment, and the tolerance is +5%.

- Difference = 3
- 3 / 20 = 0.15, so +15%

+15% breaches the +5% guardrail, so the change should not ship as it is. Rounding: whole percent.

**In the interview.** "A discount banner raises conversion by 4% relative. What else would you check?" A good answer: margin per order, average order value, returns and repeat purchases.

**Common mistakes.**

- Treating guardrails as success metrics. A guardrail only has to stay within its tolerance.
- Reading "not significantly worse" as "no harm". If the test lacked power for the guardrail, show that it is non-inferior within the tolerance.
- Choosing the guardrails after seeing the results.
